stem.en: Why can a glacial lake outburst flood reach a valley so suddenly?

text.en: A weak natural dam fails, and a whole lake empties.

feedback.en: Yes. Water that built up over years is released in a very short time.

text.en: River water rises slowly over many weeks of steady rain.

feedback.en: That would give a slow flood. A GLOF comes from a dam giving way.

text.en: Snow across the whole valley melts in the same hour.

feedback.en: Snow does not melt like that. The water here was already stored in a lake.

text.en: Sea water is pushed up the mountain valley by the tide.

feedback.en: Tides do not reach high mountain valleys. The water comes from a glacial lake.

explanation.en: Melting glaciers fill lakes behind dams of ice or loose moraine. Such a dam can give way when something strikes the lake or weakens it. The stored water is then released all at once and floods the valley downstream.

hints.en: Think about what was holding the water back.
